title: Where Creative Ideas Really Come From
desc: After three weeks of failed sketches, an idea arrives in the shower. Where did it come from? In this calm, sourced sleep-friendly deep dive we follow one imagined illustrator, Mira, and look at what science says about creative ideas: the eureka myth, the four stages of thought, Poincaré on a bus, why we get stuck, why stepping away helps, the wandering mind, walking, the aha moment in the brain, sleeping on it, and the creative edge of sleep. The second half is a long, gentle wind-down to help you fall asleep.
plan: b01: hook. Mira (an imagined illustrator, say so) is stuck for three weeks; gives up, takes a shower, the idea (a girl who collects lost sounds in jars) arrives. Overview list. Myth of the flash vs ideas as seeds.
b02: Archimedes and the eureka story (told by Vitruvius about two centuries later); Muses and ideas from outside; first verdict: the flash is real, the nowhere is not.
b03: Graham Wallas, The Art of Thought (1926): preparation, incubation, illumination, verification; Mira on the map.
b04: Henri Poincaré, Science and Method (1908): Fuchsian functions, the omnibus step at Coutances, unconscious work needs conscious effort first; certainty is a promise, not a proof.
b05: why we get stuck: Duncker's candle problem (1945), functional fixedness, Luchins' water jars (1942), Smith, Ward & Schumacher (1993) example fixation; forgetting can help.
b06: incubation evidence: Sio & Ormerod (2009) meta-analysis: positive effect, larger for divergent tasks, longer preparation helps, low-demand tasks help; why breaks work.
b07: mind wandering: Baird et al. (2012): only the undemanding-task group improved on unusual uses; why the shower works; dreamer and editor networks.

b08: walking: Oppezzo & Schwartz (2014), 176 people, 100/95/88/81 percent of walkers more creative, doubled novel responses in one experiment, residual effect when seated, mainly for many-answer thinking.
b09: the aha moment: Jung-Beeman, Kounios et al. (2004) compound word puzzles, right anterior superior temporal gyrus, gamma burst about 0.3 s before insight answers.
b10: sleeping on it: Kekule's snake story (told in 1890); Wagner et al. (2004) Sleep inspires insight: 59% vs about 23% found the hidden shortcut after 8 h sleep vs wake.
b11: the edge of sleep: Edison spheres story; Lacaux et al. (2021): 103 people, bottle in hand, N1 83% vs wake 31% vs N2 14%; at least 15 s of N1 tripled the chance; don't trade sleep for ideas.
b12: three myths: right/left-brained people (2013 PLoS ONE scan study), group brainstorming (Diehl & Stroebe 1987, production blocking), creativity as a rare gift (Simonton, quantity and quality).
b13: Mira's morning: verification, overnight extras; recap of the four stages; transition into the wind-down.
b14: wind-down 1: tonight's thoughts placed in ten glass jars on a shelf.
b15: wind-down 2: slow breathing (4 in, 6 out), a meadow at dusk, a stream.
b16: wind-down 3: body scan, softening from head to feet.
b17: wind-down 4: kindness to unfinished ideas as seeds in a winter garden; rain on the roof of a sleeping house.
b18: wind-down 5: lantern walk through a quiet wood to a starlit clearing.
b19: wind-down 6: floating over a sleeping town, thank you, Mira's book, @end teasing 'Why Music Gives You Chills'.
